issues.description: The parameter type of Pneumatic.raisePressure is inconsistent across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement specifies raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int), the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease), while the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int pressureIncrease). This mismatch will confuse students about which signature to implement and causes the solution code to be internally inconsistent (interface vs implementations).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the raisePressure parameter type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) to match the UML/problem statement and ensure LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement that int signature. Alternatively, if double is intended, update the UML/problem statement and the template instructions to specify double and change the implementing classes to use double as well.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines the Pneumatic.raisePressure method with an int parameter (pressureIncrease: int), but the provided solution interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease). This creates an API mismatch between the problem specification and the solution (and between the interface and its implementing classes in the solution), causing confusion for students about the expected method signature and likely leading to compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic.raisePressure signature across artifacts. Change the solution (and template) interface to use int raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) to match the UML/problem statement, and ensure all implementing classes override the method with the same int parameter type. Alternatively, if double is intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify double consistently.
